title: RunCase
description: One case of a run's tree, as the runtime reads the run's store when a client asks for the view CasesOfRun: the Loom runtime answers it from Loom's tree status of the store, which it reads without holding it, so it answers while the run goes on; the stub runtime has no tree and answers none. No path of the store or of a case file is in a row. The language cannot read a store, so no command creates or changes a row, as with Runbook.

case_id.description: The case's id in the run's tree.

parent.description: The case that opened this one; absent for the root.

name.description: The name the opening action gave the case (its link name); absent for the root.

protocol.description: The id of the case's protocol.

case_state.description: Where the case stands when the daemon reads the tree. Not `state`: that member of an entity is its lifecycle, and no command moves a case.

outcome.description: The outcome the case ended through; absent while it is not ended.

sdc.daemon.CaseKey.title: CaseKey
sdc.daemon.CaseKey.description: One case of one run as a row of RunCase: the run's id and the case's id. A type of its own, not RunId, because a row is a case and not the run.

sdc.daemon.CaseState.title: CaseState
sdc.daemon.CaseState.description: Where a case stands as the daemon reads its run's tree: Ended when it has an outcome; else SpendCapReached, CallCapReached or WallCapReached when the daemon ended the run at that cap (its outcome `stopped: spend cap`, `stopped: llm calls` or `stopped: wall time`), whatever the case's last stop; else AwaitingPerson or AwaitingAuthority when its last stop waits on that and the run waits on a decision; else Stuck when its last stop is Stuck or BudgetSpent and the run ended by its tree (Ended and not orphaned; a wait or a cancel that ended with the run, or an orphaned run, leaves it Open); else Running when the run's step in flight names the case; else Open. A type and not a lifecycle: no command moves a case, the daemon reads where it stands.

sdc.daemon.RunId.title: RunId
sdc.daemon.RunId.description: The id of a run. The daemon mints it (a UUID, version 7) in the HTTP handler and returns it in the answer to the submit; the handler fills the `run_id` input of SubmitRun and a client never chooses it. The state directory of the run is named after it. A run id that is already taken cannot occur, because the daemon mints it; the specification has no refusal for it.
